prompt.en: A neighbour reports RF noise in a borrowed audio device. Which first response best matches the lesson's safety and permission guidance?

text.en: Schedule brief tests, write down the conditions, and try reversible external checks before any internal work.
Open the speaker immediately and solder suppression parts in place, because internal changes are the quickest reversible test.
Run full-power checks without warning so the neighbour can decide later whether the symptom changed.
Make permanent changes to the neighbour's wiring first so later tests have a stable baseline.

explanation.en: The lesson's process starts with consent, short scheduled tests, written observations, and reversible external steps. Internal or permanent changes need permission, qualifications, and a clear reason.

prompt.en: During a scheduled troubleshooting session, a team changes transmitter power, antenna position, and the affected device's cable layout before the next trial. The symptom stops. What is the most careful conclusion?

text.en: Several variables changed at once, so the result supports more controlled testing rather than crediting one specific cure.
The transmitter was definitely producing spurious emissions because any improvement proves a transmitter fault.
The antenna position must be the only cure because it was part of the successful trial.
The affected device is proven immune now, so repeating the same conditions is unnecessary.

explanation.en: Bundled changes are useful for reducing the immediate symptom, but they do not identify which variable mattered. Change one condition at a time when assigning cause or choosing a lasting cure.

prompt.en: A log note says, 'The noise happened during my transmission, so my transmitter is dirty and receiver-side checks are unnecessary.' What is the error in that note?

text.en: Timing is useful evidence, but it does not by itself separate a transmitter fault from a pickup or overload path in the affected equipment.
The note should assume receiver-side trouble only, because a legal amateur station can never produce unwanted energy.
The note should skip the log and replace transmitter stages first, because written observations slow down repairs.
The note should treat any single report as proof that all nearby receivers will show the same symptom.

explanation.en: The lesson separates evidence from blame. A symptom that follows transmitting deserves controlled tests, but the path may be a transmitter fault, receiver overload, audio pickup, or another coupling route.
